summary: The reader has completed an undergraduate computer science degree: discrete mathematics through modular arithmetic, primes, gcds and the Euclidean algorithm, and the binary (radix) representation of integers; a first course in linear algebra over the reals covering vector spaces, bases, dimension, matrices, rank and invertibility; and the basics of complex numbers and roots of unity. They have not studied finite fields beyond GF(2), bilinear forms, tensor products, rings beyond polynomials, or the fast Fourier transform as a specialist topic, so those are explained by the wiki.

known.name: Positional (radix) representation of integers
known.gloss: A nonnegative integer written as a string of digits in a fixed base q, with each digit weighted by a power of q according to its position.

known.name: Logarithm
known.gloss: The logarithm log_b x is the exponent to which the base b must be raised to give x; lg n denotes the base-2 logarithm, rounded up to an integer in the sources.

known.name: Modular arithmetic
known.gloss: Arithmetic on integers in which two integers are identified when their difference is divisible by m, so that sums and products are computed on residues in {0, ..., m-1}.

known.name: Greatest common divisor and coprimality
known.gloss: The gcd of two integers is the largest integer dividing both, and two integers are coprime when their gcd is 1; pairwise coprime means every pair in a list is coprime.

known.name: Euclidean algorithm and modular inverses
known.gloss: The Euclidean algorithm computes the gcd of two integers by repeated division, and its extended form finds integers s, t with sa + tb = gcd(a, b), which gives inverses of a modulo b when the gcd is 1.

known.name: Prime numbers
known.gloss: A prime is an integer greater than 1 whose only positive divisors are 1 and itself, and every integer greater than 1 factors uniquely as a product of primes.

known.name: Roots of unity
aliases: powers of a root of unity
known.gloss: A complex number z is a q-th root of unity when z^q = 1, and it is primitive when its powers z^0, ..., z^(q-1) are all distinct.

known.name: Vector space, subspace, basis and dimension
known.gloss: A vector space is a set closed under addition and scalar multiplication; a subspace is a subset that is itself a vector space, and a basis is a linearly independent spanning set whose size is the dimension.

known.name: Matrix, linear map, rank and invertibility
known.gloss: A matrix represents a linear map between finite-dimensional vector spaces; its rank is the dimension of its image, and it is invertible exactly when it has full rank and a two-sided inverse.

known.name: Dot product and orthogonality
known.gloss: The dot product of two real or complex vectors is the sum of the products of their coordinates, and two vectors are orthogonal when their dot product is zero.

known.name: Field of two elements
known.gloss: The field with elements 0 and 1 in which addition is XOR (addition modulo 2) and multiplication is AND, the arithmetic of bits used in parity and Boolean computation.
